body:
### Fixed
- **Tasks without a check command no longer hang in validating.** v0.2.2 began publishing these tasks as draft pull requests, but a database safety check still allowed publishing only after a passed check. The worker retried that refused step every few seconds without logging anything, so tasks stayed in "validating" indefinitely. A task whose check was skipped because no command is configured now opens its draft pull request with the "Not validated" warning.
- These still cannot be published:
  - a failed or cancelled check;
  - a skipped check that had a command;
  - an attempt without a check step.

### Upgrade
- **No migrations, no new settings.**
- **Stuck tasks recover on their own:** after upgrading, they move on and open their draft pull requests within seconds, with no manual repair.
- **Alternative to upgrading:** set a check command (or use **Suggest a check**), then retry the stuck tasks.

### Validation
- **Repository tests against a real database** cover three cases:
  - a skipped check with no command reaches publishing, and its publication records no check;
  - a skipped check that had a command is refused;
  - an agent's own success without a check is refused.
- The updated test failed before the fix with the same refusal seen on a running install.
- The full backend suite passed on a fresh database.
- All PR CI result gates passed.

PR: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/105

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.2.2...v0.2.3

### Features
- **Preview and ports from chat:** ask the assistant to start a task's preview or expose a port, for example "expose port 3000 on ENG-12". An approval card shows the machine, the port and who can open the link. After you approve, an **Open** link appears in chat. Stopping a preview and listing ports need no approval.
- **Run a check on demand:** run a task's check from chat or with the new **Run check** button on the task card, without starting an agent attempt or changing the task. Results stream live on the task card. The assistant reports pass or fail, the exit code and the end of the output. A custom command needs permission to edit development settings.
- **Live messages with a running agent:** tell a running agent something from chat ("tell ENG-12 to also add tests") or from the new **Live messages** thread on the task card.
  - **Delivery:** Claude Code receives the message after its next tool call, through a Kuayle hook. Codex and OpenCode are told to check their inbox between steps.
  - **Replies:** the agent's replies and questions appear in chat, and questions are also sent to Telegram when it is linked.
  - **Safety:** agent text is always shown as untrusted text, and the assistant never acts on it unless you ask.
- **Settings → Assistant:** a new page with three tabs.
  - **Tools:** every assistant tool, whether it needs approval, and an on/off switch for owners and admins. A switched-off tool is not offered to the assistant, is refused if it is called anyway, and a pending approval for it fails.
  - **Skills:** Markdown instructions the assistant follows, workspace-wide or for one team. Admins can edit them with a preview, review a draft as a diff before activating it, browse version history and restore, and delete. The assistant sees only skill names and loads a skill when it is relevant. Skills it proposes stay drafts until an admin activates them.
  - **Custom tools:** scripts (sh, bash, node or python3) with typed parameters that the assistant can call. Admins build parameters with a form, test-run a tool on a machine, and see each tool's run history and versions. Tools the assistant proposes stay drafts until an admin activates them.
- **Custom tool runs:** a run uses the task machine's credential-free check container, with egress through the proxy.
  - **Arguments** arrive only as data, as environment variables and a JSON file, and are never pasted into the script.
  - **Approval:** each run needs approval unless an admin marked the tool read-only.
- **Unchecked work becomes a draft pull request:** a task with no check command no longer stops as blocked. Kuayle opens a **draft** pull request whose description starts with a "Not validated" warning. If the check later passes, that warning is replaced.
- **Check suggestion:** **Suggest a check** in the workspace, team and project development settings reads the repository's manifests and proposes a check command that needs no database (Go, npm, pnpm, yarn, Cargo, Makefile, Python). You review it and save.

### Improvements
- New tools appear in Settings → Assistant automatically, and every tool follows the workspace switches.
- The task card's check row says when a change was published without a check, and how to add one.
- Telegram answers approvals for previews, ports, checks and custom tools, and names saved skill and tool drafts.

### Fixed
- Tasks without a check command left the agent's work unpushed on the machine.

### Upgrade
- **Migrations:** applies database migrations 94 to 100. Back up the database first; the updater does this before migrating.
- **Images:** Dev Machine images must be updated to this release. The Claude Code agent image adds the live-message hook, and every agent image adds the updated agent instructions.
- **No new settings:** none are required. Optionally, add a check command, or use **Suggest a check**, so tasks open ready pull requests instead of drafts.

### Validation
- **Automated tests:**
  - The full backend suite, on a fresh database, for every merged change.
  - The browser suite, plus unit tests and type checks.
- **Unit and integration tests** cover:
  - approval and authorization paths, including team isolation and owner/admin writes;
  - tool switches that are enforced on calls and approvals;
  - draft-only proposals;
  - custom tool argument safety: shell metacharacters reach sh, bash, node and python3 scripts as plain text;
  - the live channel's read-only inbox outside the worktree, live outbox collection and the Claude Code hook script.
- All PR CI result gates passed on each final commit, including image builds and scans on amd64 and arm64.
- **Not yet verified end to end:** a live message picked up by a signed-in Claude Code session, and a custom tool run in a real Docker container. Script-level tests and fake-Docker tests cover both.

PRs: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/95, #96, #97, #98, #99, #100, #101, #102, #103, #104

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.2.1...v0.2.2

### Features
- **Task machine size:** machines Kuayle creates for agent tasks now take their size from a new *Task machines* setting in Settings → Dev Machines → Policy. The default is 4 vCPU, 8 GB and 20 GB. On these machines the coding agent gets half the memory, or 35% when Docker is on (4 GB or 2.8 GB on the default size), instead of 1.4 GB.
- **Resize machines:** change the CPU, memory and disk of an existing machine from its page. Running machines are updated live, without a restart. Shrinking the disk is allowed when current usage fits.
- **Resource-limit alerts:** when a container runs out of memory, Kuayle says so, for example "Out of memory: the agent container reached its 1.4 GiB memory limit". The message appears on the run, as the task's failure reason, in the logs and on the machine page next to Resize. A full monitored disk is reported the same way.
- **Sudo in machines:** an opt-in, admin-only *Allow sudo on new machines* policy, off by default. Terminal and IDE containers then get passwordless sudo and a writable system disk. They stay unprivileged, without network-admin or system-admin rights, and still go through the egress proxy. Agent task containers never get sudo.

### Improvements
- **Disk sizes:** any disk size in 2 GB steps from 20 GB to 2 TB, for machines and for the workspace maximum.
- **Repository settings are reused:** delegation, the assistant and the create-machine dialog use the repository configured on the issue, project, team or workspace instead of asking for it. The assistant shows the repository it chose on the approval card.
- **CLI upgrades without sudo:** global npm installs, such as `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` and `claude update`, now work on every machine. They go to a folder in the workspace that survives restarts.
- **Chat scrolling:** after you press Enter, the chat scrolls to your message and follows the reply. Scrolling up while a reply streams keeps your place and shows "Scroll to latest".
- **Installed app:** zooming is disabled when Kuayle runs as an installed app. Browser tabs keep normal zoom.

### Fixed
- Agent tasks on small machines were killed for running out of memory, with no explanation.
- The installer test now reads the pinned digest from the script, so release version bumps no longer break it.

### Upgrade
- Applies database migrations 90, 91 and 93. Back up the database first; the updater does this before migrating.
- Existing workspaces get the new task machine default (8 GB). Machines that already exist keep their size, and can now be resized.
- Dev Machine images must be updated to this release, for the npm folder in the workspace and sudo support.
- Disk resize needs the default monitored disk quota mode. Hard XFS quotas are fixed when a volume is created.

### Validation
- **Automated tests:**
  - Full backend suite on a fresh database.
  - The browser suite (270 tests), plus unit tests and type checks.
- **Real Docker tests** confirmed that:
  - sudo containers have root but no network-admin or system-admin rights, and cannot reach the network without the proxy;
  - locked containers cannot use sudo;
  - `docker update` resizes running and stopped containers;
  - an out-of-memory kill is detected.
- **Self-hosted preview:**
  - sudo and a global npm install without sudo worked;
  - a running machine was resized from 1 vCPU / 2 GB to 2 vCPU / 4 GB live;
  - an out-of-memory kill in the terminal was reported on the machine;
  - the issue's inherited repository was resolved;
  - the workspace disk limit accepted 62 GB and rejected 63.
- All PR CI result gates passed, including image builds and vulnerability scans on amd64 and arm64.

PR: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/94

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.2.0...v0.2.1

### Features
- **AI assistant chat:** persistent, private conversations with streaming replies, folders, rename, project tags and a project filter. The assistant can find, create, plan, split and link issues, delegate coding work, request reviews and merge or accept work, always behind an approval for changes. It also works from Telegram (text, photos and voice notes).
- **Coding agents on Dev Machines:** issues are delegated to Codex, Claude Code or other supported agents. Each task runs in its own worktree through validation and publication to a pull request, and completes on merge or when you accept it in Kuayle. Follow-up attempts come from CI failures, change requests and issue comments. Tasks wait for their blockers, and agent sessions resume natively.
- **Agent collaboration:** agents on related issues can message each other as issue comments or internally. Every message is kept in Settings → Agent messages, where admins and task creators can hold, release or drop them.
- **App ports for manual QA:** any number of ports per machine, each on its own authenticated address. Listening ports are detected automatically, and each task can start and stop its own app.
- **Full Docker Compose:** an optional, sandboxed rootless Docker daemon per machine (workspace policy *Allow Docker on new machines*, off by default) runs real `docker compose` projects; their published ports become app ports.
- **Model servers and agent configuration:** any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint, with models fetched automatically, plus sign-in support for agents that use their own accounts.
- **Voice and images:** dictation with a self-hosted transcription service (faster-whisper or Vosk) and image attachments for vision-capable models.
- **Installable app:** Kuayle can be installed as a PWA when served over HTTPS.

### Improvements
- Dev Machines moved into Settings, with Machines, Policy and Automations tabs. Machines can run up to 20 per user and work with several repositories.
- Diff panel beside the chat, task cards with compact actions, and a live connection status.
- Terminal rendering fixes (WebGL renderer, joined box-drawing lines, resize forwarding).

### Security
- Agent attempts never receive push credentials; publication, reviews and merges are performed by Kuayle under the current permissions, and agent output is always treated as untrusted.
- Image advisories with available fixes are resolved (including Docker CLI 29.9.2, Compose 5.6.1 and Buildx 0.38.1 built from source, and a rebuilt runc and containerd shim). The remaining advisories have no upstream fix yet and are accepted only through `.trivyignore.yaml`, per package version, until 2027-01-31.

### Upgrade
- Applies database migrations 53–89. Back up the database first. The updater does this before migrating.
- Re-run `selfhosting/gateway-role.sql` after migrating, because the machine gateway reads new columns.
- Optional services and settings, all documented in `selfhosting/.env.example`:
  - the voice service (`VOICE_URL`, `VOICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN`);
  - the machine Docker daemon (`DEV_MACHINE_DOCKER_IMAGE`, `DEV_MACHINE_DOCKER_RUNTIME`, and the seccomp/AppArmor profiles).
- Dev Machine images must be updated to this release.

### Validation
- Full backend suite passed. The browser suite passed with 250 tests, plus unit tests and type checks.
- Verified end to end on a self-hosted preview with a real GitHub repository and Codex on DeepSeek:
  - delegation through review and merge;
  - accepting without a merge;
  - two agents exchanging messages;
  - a Compose project with a build served through an app port;
  - per-task apps and Telegram.
- All PR CI result gates passed, including image builds and vulnerability scans on amd64 and arm64.

PR: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/93

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.1.37...v0.2.0

### Fixed
- Fixed a machine-manager crash when GitHub App credentials are configured per workspace instead of globally. Repository operations now use the workspace credentials correctly.
- This also fixes release updates getting left in maintenance mode when the manager crashed during startup health checks.
- Updated CLI pin validation tests to support automatic version refreshes while still requiring concrete versions and architecture checksums.

### Upgrade
No database migrations or configuration changes. This release includes the permanent fix for the manager startup crash.

PR: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/92

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.1.36...v0.1.37

### Self-hosting
- **Clearer System update status:** Settings → Version now shows whether the updater is connected and how its last run ended (in progress, completed or failed), with timestamps. The confirmation dialog no longer shows the shell command.
- **Failure reasons:** a failed update shows why it failed, and a **Failure details** section expands to the updater's recent output.
- **Everyone sees the upgrade page:** when an update starts, every connected browser goes to the "Upgrade in progress" page. The page returns to where each user was once the update ends.
- **Upgrade page logo:** the logo is now embedded in the page, so it shows on every URL, including deep links such as `/workspace/settings/version`.

### Upgrade
No database migrations or configuration changes. The update scripts do not replace the running updater sidecar. To get failure details, rebuild and recreate the `updater` service once, using the same Compose project and files you deploy with.

PR: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/91

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.1.35...v0.1.36

### Improvements
- Release publication now automatically refreshes all seven built-in agent CLIs: Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Qwen Code, Crush, Goose, and Kimi.
- Exact versions remain pinned across the shared installer and runtime Dockerfiles. Goose and Kimi checksums are refreshed for both amd64 and arm64.
- Release runtime builds and scans use the exact refreshed source commit. Invalid or incomplete upstream metadata stops the refresh before any pins are changed.

### Upgrade
No database migrations or configuration changes. CLI updates take effect when runtime images are rebuilt and new containers use them; existing running machines are not modified automatically.

PR: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/90

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.1.34...v0.1.35

### Improvements
- **Upgrade directly from the release notice:** the new-version modal now includes an **Upgrade now** button that opens Settings → Version at the System update controls in the current workspace. The notice closes and stays dismissed after navigation.
- The button supports keyboard navigation and mobile layouts, with labels in English, Italian, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese.

### Upgrade
No database migrations or configuration changes. Starting an update still requires system-admin access and the existing confirmation.

### Validation
- All 166 frontend browser tests and 43 unit tests passed.
- Web and all-in-one images passed build, runtime smoke tests, and vulnerability scans on amd64 and arm64.
- All four PR CI result gates passed.

PR: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/89

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.1.33...v0.1.34

### Self-hosting
- **Updates from pinned release deployments:** Settings → Version updates now work on production installs that run a detached release checkout with digest-pinned images. An opt-in release updater picks the latest stable release, pulls the API and UI images by release tag and records their digests, and rebuilds active Dev Machines components without changing the checkout. Images are prepared before downtime, and the database is backed up before migrations. If a migration or health check fails, maintenance mode stays on and writers stay stopped. Running the update again on a current deployment verifies it without restarting. By @carbogninalberto in https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/87
- **Upgrade page logo:** the logo on the "Upgrade in progress" page now loads on any URL, not only `/`. By @carbogninalberto in https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/88

### Upgrade
No database migrations. The release updater is opt-in; source-build deployments keep their existing update path.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.1.32...v0.1.33

Security release. A full audit of authorization, sessions, Dev Machines, input handling, the frontends and the supply chain found and fixed two high-severity and five medium-severity issues. Upgrading is recommended for all installations.

### Security
- **Asset links could run script (high):** a workspace import could give an attachment an executable content type, which an uploaded SVG could load through a public asset link and run as the viewer. Attachments are now served only with an allowed file type; anything else downloads as a file.
- **Shared GitHub App installations could be claimed (high):** with one GitHub App shared by all workspaces, a workspace owner could connect another account's unlinked installation. Kuayle now confirms that the installing GitHub user can access the installation.
- **Signing out now ends API access:** a refresh token could be used as an access token for seven days, including after sign-out.
- **AI settings can no longer reach internal addresses:** the AI provider URL was able to send requests from the server to private networks. Requests now go only to public addresses and never follow redirects.
- **Workspace isolation:**
  - Unlinking a GitHub repository can no longer affect another workspace.
  - Issues, projects and templates now accept only members, labels, cycles and statuses from their own workspace.
- **GitHub webhook bodies are limited** to GitHub's 25 MB maximum.

The full report, including lower-severity items that remain open, is in [SECURITY_AUDIT.md](https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/blob/main/SECURITY_AUDIT.md).

### Upgrade
No database migrations. Existing sign-ins keep working.
- **Shared GitHub App** (`GITHUB_APP_ID` set): in the GitHub App settings, enable **Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation**, and set `GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID` and `GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_SECRET`. Until then, new installations are refused. Existing connections and per-workspace apps are unaffected.
- **AI provider on a private or local network:** set `AI_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK=true`. Every workspace owner can then make the server call internal addresses.
- Assignees and labels from another workspace are now ignored instead of attached.

### Validation
- Full Go suite with race detection against a freshly migrated PostgreSQL, with a regression test for each fix.
- Frontend type checks, unit tests, and the full Playwright suite (162 tests); website checks.
- `govulncheck` and `npm audit` (production): no known vulnerabilities. Secret scan of the full git history: test fixtures only.
- Release images and all Dev Machine images built, smoke-tested and scanned for HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities on amd64 and arm64.
- PR: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/86

Dev Machines gain more agent CLIs, a lighter headless machine type, workspace DeepSeek support for Codex and Claude Code, and a terminal that renders full-screen TUIs properly.

### New
- **More agent CLIs:** **Qwen Code**, **Crush**, **Kimi** and **Goose** join Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex. They are installed in every developer image and can be selected per machine and per agent run.
  - Admins enable them in Dev Machine settings; existing workspaces keep their current provider list until then.
  - Pi is not included yet: its latest release has an unfixed HIGH-severity CVE.
- **Headless machines:** a terminal plus all agent CLIs, with no code editor or browser.
  - The terminal gets half of the machine's CPU and memory.
  - Headless machines can also run autonomous agent runs.
- **DeepSeek for Codex and Claude Code:**
  - Workspace admins store one encrypted DeepSeek API key, with a default model (`deepseek-flash` or `deepseek-v4-pro`) and thinking level (off, low, high, max).
  - Codex and Claude Code in every machine use it automatically, and Codex's `/model` picker lists only the DeepSeek models.
  - Each agent run can override the model and thinking level.
- **Full-screen terminal:** a button or `Ctrl+Shift+F`. Escape is left to the running program.

### Improvements
- **Terminal:**
  - Codex, Claude Code and OpenCode render correctly, including prompt symbols, box drawing and logos.
  - Text selection and copy work.
  - Mouse movement no longer types stray characters.
  - Rendering uses WebGL, falling back automatically when WebGL is unavailable.
- **Subscription sign-in:**
  - API keys for Claude Code and Codex are now optional, so you can sign in with a subscription from the terminal (`codex login`, or `/login` in Claude).
  - Sign-ins are stored in the machine's temporary home directory: they are lost when the machine stops or pauses, and are not available to agent runs.
- **Codex's background server starts:** Codex 0.160 no longer fails with `Permission denied` in machine terminals. Machines created before this release get the fix when their containers are recreated.

### Security
- Crush is built from source with patched Go 1.27.3, because its release binaries embed a Go standard library with known CVEs.
- Qwen Code's bundled `sharp` is upgraded to 0.35.5 (GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w).
- The headless image ships without a C toolchain, which keeps unfixable kernel-header CVEs out of it.

### Upgrade
Back up the database, run `./server migrate up`, and rebuild the runtime images (`docker compose --profile dev-machine-images build`; `selfhosting/update.sh` does this when Dev Machines are active).
- Migration 51 adds the machine profile and expands only the *default* provider list.
- Migration 52 adds the encrypted workspace DeepSeek credential and per-run model settings.
- New optional setting: `DEV_MACHINE_HEADLESS_IMAGE` (default `ghcr.io/kuayle/dev-machine-headless:0.1.0`).

### Validation
- Full Go suite against a freshly migrated PostgreSQL, including the up → down → up round trips of migrations 51 and 52.
- Frontend type checks, unit tests, and the full Playwright suite (161 tests).
- IDE and headless images: builds, smoke tests and Trivy HIGH/CRITICAL scans on amd64 and arm64.
- Live Docker stack checks:
  - headless machines starting with only terminal, collector and egress containers;
  - a Goose autonomous run;
  - Codex reaching the DeepSeek API through the generated configuration.
- PR: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/85 (includes #82)

Issue templates now use the same focused workflow as issue creation. Templates can be edited from settings, include a rich-text description and issue properties, and keep a separate display title and default issue title.

### Improvements

- Add a visible edit action and an issue-style create/edit dialog for templates.
- Add a rich-text template description plus team, status, priority, assignee, and label defaults.
- Keep the template title separate from the editable issue title that is prefilled when applying the template.
- Preserve custom issue titles with **Create more** and keep team, status, cycle, project, and attachment ownership consistent when applying templates.
- Restrict sub-issue templates to shared templates or templates owned by the parent issue team.
- Add migration 50 for `default_issue_title`, with API validation and backward-compatible fallback to the template title.

### Upgrade

Self-hosted installations should back up the database and run `./server migrate up` before using the new template fields. Existing templates remain valid; their issue-title fallback continues to use the template title.

### Validation

- Full Go suite with race detection
- Frontend type checks and template/issue-navigation Playwright suites
- PostgreSQL migration validation
- Release Readiness images and smoke tests on amd64 and arm64
- PR: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/80

Fix permanent Dev Machine deletion after IDE or gateway access creates audit entries. Migration 49 clears dependent references together, preserving audit history and workspace ownership checks. Workspace deletion receives the same correction.

Validated against PostgreSQL with existing access logs, transaction rollback, service and workspace deletion, migration downgrade/upgrade, and cross-workspace integrity checks.

Self-hosted upgrades must run database migrations (`./server migrate up`) before relying on the corrected cleanup behavior. Back up the database before upgrading.

- Fix: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/84
- Same-site Dev Machines and automatic HTTPS introduced in v0.1.28: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/releases/tag/v0.1.28

## Dev Machines for personal instances

- Explicit same-site hosting with `DEV_MACHINE_ALLOW_SAME_SITE=true`, keeping separate domains as the default.
- HTTPS-only configuration, host-prefixed session cookies, and exact-origin protection for browser mutations and WebSocket upgrades. Sign in again when enabling the option.
- Private certificate approval for stock Caddy on-demand HTTPS: wildcard DNS can work with any DNS provider, without DNS API credentials. Certificates are approved only for running machine services.

## Security and maintenance

- Update Echo to 4.16.1 and code-server to 4.143.1.
- Refresh Undici, body-parser and Zod dependencies; preserve Zod v3 consumers and backport collection-bound protection with regression tests.

No database migration. See the README's personal-instance setup for configuration and certificate rate-limit considerations.

Implemented and reviewed in #83.

## What's Changed

- **Dev Machines without XFS (monitored disk mode):** Set `DEV_MACHINE_DISK_QUOTA_MODE=monitored` to run Dev Machines on hosts whose Docker data root has no XFS project quotas (for example ext4). Workspace disk limits are then measured every 30 seconds instead of enforced by the kernel. Machines warn at 90 %, stop at 100 %, and all machines stop (with new starts refused) when the host's free space falls below a configurable floor. Administrators see a banner in Dev Machine settings, and machine pages label the limit as monitored. Hard mode remains the default.
- **Custom machine sizes:** Choose vCPU, memory and disk with sliders that snap to sensible values, instead of fixed Small/Medium/Large presets. Memory stays at least 1 GB per vCPU and disk within the workspace limit. Environment Builders now open the same resource dialog.
- **Clearer limits:** Machines that never started and are no longer wanted no longer count towards workspace or per-user limits. Quota errors say which limit was reached and how to proceed.
- **Disk usage visibility:** Machine pages highlight workspace disk usage at 90 % or more of the limit.

## Upgrade Notes

- Migration `000048` allows the new `custom` machine size; its rollback converts custom machines to `large`.
- The self-hosting Compose file now mounts Docker's data root read-only into the machine manager (`DEV_MACHINE_DOCKER_ROOT`, default `/var/lib/docker`) and passes `DEV_MACHINE_DISK_QUOTA_MODE`, `DEV_MACHINE_HOST_DISK_MIN_FREE_PERCENT` (15) and `DEV_MACHINE_HOST_DISK_MIN_FREE_GB` (25).
- Existing installations stay in hard mode unless they opt in. In monitored mode a fast writer can briefly exceed its limit between checks, so size the free-space floor to absorb that.

[PR #81](https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/81) · [Disk limitation docs](https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/blob/main/TECHNICAL.md#disk-limitation)

**Full Changelog:** https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.1.26...v0.1.27

## Validation

PR #81 passed all of its CI jobs on `824d070`, including:
- backend tests against PostgreSQL;
- Docker runtime integration;
- every Dev Machine image and every release image (amd64 and arm64);
- the frontend, Go and updater security scans;
- self-hosting checks.

UI: 42 unit tests and 144 browser tests. Candidate `277d7ae` (the merge commit on `main`) passed the full Tests and Security Scan runs. The publishing workflow updates version files on `main`. If its resulting commit differs from this candidate, revalidate that commit before rollout.

## What's Changed

- **Original UI design restored (KUA-63):** Buttons, fields and selects migrated in v0.1.25 regain their original size, padding, alignment, colors and hover states. They still use the shared shadcn-svelte foundation, through a new opt-in `plain` variant.
- **Sidebar:** Team rows and section headings are left-aligned with navigation again. Expanded sections no longer show a permanent grey highlight, and keyboard focus wraps the whole header row as before. Drag-reorder and the collapsed drawer are unchanged.
- **Issue lists:** Group headers lose the new grey bars and thick focus ring. Clicking anywhere in the checkbox area selects an issue, including Shift-click ranges, instead of opening it. Rows are keyboard-focusable again.
- **Issue title:** The issue-creation title is back to its prominent, borderless 18px style.
- **Login and password fields:** The reveal (eye) toggle is vertically centered in every password field and is skipped when tabbing. The Sign in button is back to full height in the accent color.

## What's Changed

* **Private teams:** Added privacy controls and membership-based access across issues, projects, cycles, comments, attachments, and real-time updates. Access is revoked when membership is removed; workspace owners and admins retain access. By @carbogninalberto in https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/67
* **More reliable navigation:** Temporary membership-check failures no longer redirect users or leave them stuck on the splash screen. Older failed requests also no longer override a successful retry. By @carbogninalberto in https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/68
* **Safer self-hosted upgrades:** The updater stops backend writers before privacy migrations and keeps the backend stopped if a migration fails, preventing an older version from running against a partially migrated database.
* **Fixed Docker routing:** API requests, uploads, and health/readiness endpoints now reach the backend correctly instead of being intercepted by the frontend fallback.
* **Configurable build memory:** Docker UI builds now default to a configurable 4 GB Node heap.
* **Dependency fixes:** Updated `source-map-js` to address a denial-of-service flaw, refreshed vulnerable marketing-site build dependencies, and patched a code-server compression memory leak in the Dev Machines IDE image.
* **Updated self-hosting documentation:** Added private-team setup, legacy attachment handling, migration requirements, and downgrade guidance.

### Upgrade Notes

Existing teams remain public after upgrading. Enabling private teams introduces persistent workspace-wide restrictions: saved views, filtered/view-based public links, workspace export, AI expansion, outgoing webhooks, Dev Machines, and live presence are disabled—even if all teams are later made public or deleted.

Back up PostgreSQL and asset storage before upgrading. Apply migrations with backend writers stopped, and deploy the new backend and migrations together. See the [private-team documentation](https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle#private-teams) before enabling privacy.
